finding: The round-6 invariant is NOT established: the `normals != 1` rule constrains the `dir` STRING, but the function returns `candidate.canonicalize()`, and canonicalize EXPANDS a symlink. A single-component `dir` that is a symlink to a NESTED in-workspace directory therefore returns a root with model-controlled INTERMEDIATE components — exactly what round 6 claims it makes impossible. REPRO (/data/pbya/ziee/tmp/r7a, verbatim replicas of resolve_conversation_workspace_dir's path logic + open_confined's O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY anchor + openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, run on this host): setup `mkdir -p base/a/etc; echo PLANTED-DECOY > base/a/etc/passwd; ln -s a/etc base/proj`; then resolve(base,"proj") is ACCEPTED (normals=1, is_absolute=false, starts_with(base_canon)=true, is_dir=true) and returns `<base>/a/etc` — 2 model-controlled components instead of 1. Validate-time open_confined(root,"passwd") reads "PLANTED-DECOY\n". A subsequent `mv a a.bak && ln -s / a` (the round-6 attack verbatim) leaves the root path STRING unchanged, and the next open_confined(root,"passwd") returns 1373 bytes beginning "root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash" — host /etc/passwd, through the confined open. The included control proves the fix DOES work for a plain dir (swapping a non-symlink `proj` is refused with ENOTDIR by the O_NOFOLLOW anchor), so the symlink expansion is the sole residual. NO RACE IS REQUIRED: dispatch.rs:92/398 call `load_raw_prompt(&ctx.extracted_path, ...)` per step at execution time, tools.rs:575 sets the ephemeral row's `extracted_path` to this canonicalized root, and dispatch.rs:870 RW-bind-mounts `<workspace_root>/<conv>` (which contains it) as the sandbox home — so an EARLIER sandbox step of the same run performs the swap and a LATER llm step's `prompt_file:` reads the host file. The plain-dir case is genuinely sound because the remaining intermediates (`<workspace_root>`, `<conv>`) are unreachable from inside the bind; the fix is a real improvement, but incomplete. Closing it needs the returned root's components to be constrained, not the input string's — e.g. `symlink_metadata(&candidate)` rejecting a symlinked final component, or asserting `canon.parent() == Some(base_canon)`.

The new SCOPE comment on `open_confined` asserts an invariant that does not hold, and asserts it as the load-bearing justification for the whole mechanism: "which is why `resolve_conversation_workspace_dir` restricts its `dir` to a SINGLE component. With `dir = \"a/b\" the model would control `a`, an intermediate component ... The two rules are one mechanism: this refuses a swapped final component, that makes the final component the only one the model can swap." Per the repro in row 1, a single-component SYMLINKED `dir` yields a root with 2 model-controlled components, so the final component is NOT the only one the model can swap and the two rules do NOT compose into the claimed mechanism. The same false claim is repeated at workspace.rs:74-82 ("With a single component, the only model-controlled part of the root IS that final component") and in the user-facing error string at workspace.rs:101-102 ("'dir' must name a single directory directly inside the conversation workspace") — a symlinked dir resolves to a directory at arbitrary depth, so that message misdescribes what is enforced. This is the exact failure mode that produced round 6 in the first place (FIX_ROUND-6.md: "My comment claimed that attack was closed"): a future maintainer reading open_confined will conclude the intermediate-component class is handled and will not re-derive it. Reported separately from row 1 because the code fix and the comment fix are different edits and a partial fix that leaves the comment standing re-creates the same trap.

The single-component rule is a CREATION-TIME check on one surface, but the value it is supposed to constrain is PERSISTED and re-consumed by three entry points that never re-check it. `resolve_conversation_workspace_dir` runs only inside workflow_mcp/tools.rs:614/668/748 and handlers/dev.rs:1579/1624; its result is written to the DB as `workflows.extracted_path` (tools.rs:575, `insert_ephemeral_workflow`). From then on `spawn_run` (runner.rs:1251), `resume_run` (runner.rs:1559) and `run_for_test` (runner.rs:1097, the `POST /workflows/{id}/test` surface) all feed `PathBuf::from(&workflow.extracted_path)` straight into `validate_for_install_async` and into `ctx.extracted_path` -> `read_prompt_file`, with no re-derivation and no shape check. So the guard is not located where the value is used: it is a property of a transient computation, not of the string that reaches the kernel-confined open. Concretely this widens row 1 — after the ephemeral row exists, the model can swap the intermediate via a plain `code_sandbox` `execute_command` between calls and then re-enter through `/test` or `resume_run`, neither of which passes back through `resolve_conversation_workspace_dir`'s canonicalize+starts_with. It also means any future writer of `extracted_path` silently inherits zero enforcement. Verified by reading all four call sites; no `extracted_path` consumer re-validates.

The two tests shipped with the fix certify the hole as closed. `t1_confine_rejects_nested_dir` builds `base/proj/flow` as REAL directories and asserts `dir="proj/flow"` is refused — it pins only the string-shape half. `t1_confine_accepts_a_single_safe_dir` creates `base/proj` as a real directory. Neither ever creates a SYMLINK, and `grep -n symlink src/modules/workflow/workspace.rs tests/workflow_mcp/workspace_test.rs` returns only three prose comment hits and zero test code — so there is no test anywhere, unit or integration, in which `dir` names a symlink. The suite is therefore green (verified: `cargo test --lib -p ziee -- workflow::` = 191 passed / 1 failed, the 1 being the pre-existing `job_kind_parses_round_trips_and_is_orthogonal` unknown-variant `subagent` panic) against a tree in which the documented attack still succeeds. The missing test CLASS is 'the returned root, not the input string, has exactly one model-controlled component' — e.g. assert `resolve(...).unwrap().parent() == base.canonicalize()`, which fails today for a symlinked dir and would have caught row 1. Note the docstring on `t1_confine_rejects_nested_dir` itself restates the false invariant from row 2.

The MCP tool schema now contradicts the enforced contract. `dir_prop` still reads "The workspace subdir (relative to /home/sandboxuser) holding workflow.yaml + any scripts/ you wrote with the code_sandbox tools", and the RUN_FROM_WORKSPACE description still says "Write workflow.yaml (+ scripts/) into /home/sandboxuser/<dir>/ first" — neither states the new single-component requirement, and `<dir>` in prose reads as an arbitrary relative path. A model that organises its work as `projects/report/` (a natural layout, and one the old code accepted — `t1_confine_accepts_nested_safe_dir` asserted exactly that before this diff renamed it) now gets a hard WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE_BAD_DIR the schema did not predict. Rated LOW rather than MEDIUM because it is self-correcting: workflow_mcp returns the failure via `error_tool_result(e.error_code(), e.to_string())`, so the model receives the explanatory string "'dir' must name a single directory directly inside the conversation workspace, not a nested path" and can retry with a flat dir. Fix is one sentence in `dir_prop`.

REJECTED — candidate: the `Component::Normal` counting has a parsing hole. Tested all 22 candidate spellings against real `Path::components()` on this host (edition-2024 Rust, /data/pbya/ziee/tmp/r7a part A) rather than reasoning about it. Results: `proj/.`, `./proj`, `proj/`, `./proj/.`, `proj/./` all normalise to exactly 1 Normal (CurDir is dropped/tolerated) -> ACCEPT, correct. `proj//x`, `proj/./x`, `a/b` -> 2 Normals -> rejected. `.`/`./` -> 0 Normals -> rejected by `normals != 1` (this is why the check is `!= 1` and not `> 1`, and it is right). `..`, `proj/..`, `a/../b` -> ParentDir hits the `_` arm -> rejected. `//proj` -> RootDir, caught earlier by `is_absolute()`. Unicode `α`, space, `-`, and an embedded TAB are single Normals and are legitimately accepted (all legal Unix filenames, and `canonicalize` + `starts_with` still confine them). `proj\x` and `C:proj` are single Normals ON UNIX, which is correct there (backslash and colon are ordinary filename characters); on Windows `Path` splits `proj\x` into 2 Normals and parses `C:proj` as Prefix+Normal, both of which the existing arms reject. NUL cannot reach here as a path component. No bypass found in the counting itself — the defect in row 1 is downstream of it (canonicalize), not in it.

REJECTED — candidate: two SYNC `validate_collecting` calls survive in async handlers (dev.rs:107 in `validate_workflow`, dev.rs:954 in `validate_workflow_def`), so round 6's sweep is still incomplete. Rejected on inspection: both pass `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ziee-wf-validate-{}", Uuid::new_v4()))`, a freshly-generated, never-created path. `check_prompt_files` (validate.rs:1581) opens with `let bundle_present = bundle_root.is_dir();` and skips the existence/confinement half when false, so ZERO `prompt_file:` bytes are read on either path — the only blocking syscall is a single `stat` on a nonexistent path. Round 6's claim was specifically about REAL-bundle callers, and that claim now holds: every call site that passes a materialised bundle root (hub/handlers.rs:2188, dev.rs:268, dev.rs:565, runner.rs:1251, runner.rs:1559, tools.rs:543, tools.rs:689) uses an `_async` variant. The sync `validate_collecting` remaining `pub` for these two draft surfaces is correct, not a miss.

REJECTED — candidate: `validate_collecting_async` is wired wrong (error mapping / is_dev / cancellation). Checked each: (a) `is_dev` — the replaced call at tools.rs:689 was `validate_collecting(&def, &root, false)` and the new one is `validate_collecting_async(&def, &root, false).await?`; the `false` (real gate, mocks flagged) is preserved and the comment above it still says so. (b) error mapping — `spawn_blocking(...).await` yields `Result<Vec<ValidationError>, JoinError>`; a JoinError here can only be a panic in the validator or a runtime shutdown, both genuine internal faults, so `AppError::internal_error` + `?` is right, and it correctly does NOT go through `error_tool_result` (which is for author-facing verdicts; the findings themselves are returned in the Ok payload and split by severity below). Signature matches `validate_for_install_async` exactly. (c) cancellation — `spawn_blocking` work is not aborted when the MCP request future is dropped, so a cancelled call still reads the bundle to completion; that is bounded by `MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES` (1 MiB) x step count and is byte-identical to the pre-existing `validate_for_install_async` behaviour on the same root (invoked one function earlier via `load_and_validate_workspace`), so it introduces no new exposure. No defect.

REJECTED — candidate: the new nested-dir rejection breaks an existing caller, test, or e2e that legitimately passes a nested `dir`. Swept every `dir` value reaching the guard: `grep -no '"dir": *"[^"]*"' server/tests/` yields only `flow` (12x) and `ghost` (1x), all single-component; `server/tests/workflow_mcp/workspace_test.rs:190`'s rejection list is `["../../etc", "/etc", "a/../../b"]`, all of which still reject (the first two on the pre-existing absolute/ParentDir arms, the third on ParentDir before the new `normals != 1` arm is reached, so its asserted error code WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE_BAD_DIR is unchanged). E2E: `ui/tests/e2e/chat/workflow-workspace-run-card.spec.ts` uses `dir: 'flow'` and `14-split-chat/workflow-export-per-pane.spec.ts` uses `workspace_dir: 'my-wf-dir'` — both flat, and both are response fixtures that never reach the resolver. Nothing real is broken; the only behavioural regression is the un-updated tool-schema prose, filed separately as low.

REJECTED — candidate: `let base_canon = base.canonicalize().unwrap_or(base);` compares a canonicalised `canon` against a NON-canonicalised `base_canon` on the fallback branch, so a workspace root containing a symlink component (e.g. the `std::env::temp_dir()`-based fallback root at runner.rs:1786 on macOS, where /tmp -> /private/tmp) would make `canon.starts_with(&base_canon)` fail and yield a spurious WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE_ESCAPE. Rejected as unreachable: the `unwrap_or` branch is taken only when `base.canonicalize()` errors, and control cannot reach line 115 unless `candidate.canonicalize()` at line 109 already SUCCEEDED — which requires every ancestor of `candidate`, including `base`, to exist and be traversable. `base.canonicalize()` therefore cannot fail at that point, and the fallback is dead defensive code rather than a live mismatch.

REJECTED — candidate: INSTALLED (non-ephemeral) workflow bundle roots also have sandbox-writable intermediate components, which would mean the single-component rule protects only one of several producers. Traced the mount plumbing: dispatch.rs:829 stages the workflow bundle as `StagedMount { mode: StageMode::ReadOnly, host_path: ctx.sandbox_workspace, sandbox_path: run_dir }` — the run dir is RO inside the sandbox — and the only ReadWrite staging is the per-step artifacts dir (dispatch.rs:832) plus the sandbox HOME bind, which dispatch.rs:864-871 sets to `workflow_workspace_root().join(conv_id)`. Installed bundles are extracted under the workflows data dir (hub/handlers.rs:2170 `target_dir`, dev.rs:268 `extraction.extracted_path`), which is not under `<workspace_root>/<conv>` and is therefore not inside any RW bind. So `hub/handlers.rs:2188`, `dev.rs:268`, `dev.rs:565` and the `runner.rs` calls on an installed row all take roots with no model-writable component. Only the ephemeral/workspace producer puts the root inside the RW home bind — which is the one row 1 covers. The enumeration of producers is otherwise complete.

REJECTED — candidate: even for a PLAIN single-component `dir`, the root `<workspace_root>/<conv>/<dir>` still has two intermediate components (`<workspace_root>` and `<conv>`) that the model might rename, defeating the fix outright. Rejected: dispatch.rs:864-871 binds host `<workspace_root>/<conv>` AT `/home/sandboxuser`, so from inside the sandbox `..` from the workspace is the guest's own `/home`, not the host's `<workspace_root>`; the guest has no name for either the host parent directory or its own mount point, and cannot rename them. code_sandbox/tools/files.rs:33 documents the same bind ("workspace is RW-bind-mounted into the sandbox at /home/sandboxuser"). My repro's control leg confirms the complementary half empirically: with a plain non-symlink `proj`, swapping it for `ln -s /etc proj` after resolve is refused by the O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY anchor with ENOTDIR. So the plain-dir case is genuinely sound and the round-6 change is a real, load-bearing improvement — the defect in row 1 is strictly the symlink-expansion path, not the rule's premise.
